meta.notes: All props are common household items; professional equipment is prohibited. Small-part props are forbidden for under-3s (enforced by the safety filter). English mirror of references/games-library.json.

games.name: Peek-a-boo
steps: Parent covers their own face with the scarf and asks, 'Where is Mommy?'
Pull the scarf away with a big smile and an exaggerated 'Here I am!'
After 3-4 rounds, drape the scarf lightly over the baby's head and encourage the baby to pull it off
Cheer and clap the moment the baby pulls it off: 'You found me!'
games.goal: Object permanence + parent-child bonding and emotional exchange
games.safety: Never cover mouth or nose for more than a few seconds; keep one hand on the scarf corner at all times; use a thin breathable scarf
games.extensions: For older babies, hide behind a door or sofa side for them to find; hide a toy under the scarf for the baby to uncover

games.name: Cardboard Crawl Tunnel
steps: Open both ends of the box and place it on a play mat to form a tunnel
Sit at the exit and call the baby's name or shake a sound-making toy
As the baby crawls in, peek through the exit: 'Wow, I see you!'
After 3-5 rounds, prop a cushion under the entrance to add a gentle incline
games.goal: Four-limb coordination, core strength, spatial awareness
games.safety: Tape seams face outward to avoid scratches; tunnel no longer than 1.5x baby's body length; parent guards the exit at all times
games.extensions: Line the tunnel with different fabrics (fleece blanket/towel) for tactile variety; place a surprise toy at the exit

games.name: Grab-and-Drop Basket
steps: Seat the baby in the high chair and place the basket with 3-4 safe kitchen items on the tray
Demonstrate dropping the wooden spoon into the basket, saying 'In it goes'
Encourage the baby to grab an item and drop it in; praise each success
Level up: have the baby take items out and hand them to you
games.goal: Grasp-and-release control, hand-eye coordination, container concept
games.safety: All items larger than 4cm to prevent choking; no sharp edges or breakable parts; baby always within sight
games.extensions: Swap in items of different weights and textures (plastic cup/silicone bowl); add 'give one to Mommy' hand-over practice

games.name: Babble Echo Conversation
steps: During quiet pre-sleep time, lie face to face or hold the baby
Echo back any babble the baby makes with the same sounds
Pause 2-3 seconds and wait for the baby to vocalize again, forming a turn-taking dialogue
Close with a soft summary: 'You said so much today'
games.goal: Sound imitation, turn-taking awareness, parent-child attachment
games.safety: Keep the room quiet with soft lighting; never force interaction when the baby is fussy or sleepy
games.extensions: Add simple reduplicated words (mama/dada/baa-baa); repeat the game in front of a mirror during the day

games.name: Water Sensory Bag
steps: Fill the bag halfway with water, add 3-4 colorful caps, squeeze out air and double-seal
Lay the bag flat in front of the baby for patting and pressing
Guide the baby's finger to push a cap toward one corner: 'The cap is sliding away!'
Name the colors as you play: 'red cap, yellow cap'
games.goal: Cause-and-effect cognition, tactile input, early color perception
games.safety: Caps stay sealed inside the bag; reinforce the zip with tape; remove immediately if leaking; never leave unattended
games.extensions: Use lukewarm vs. cooler bags to introduce temperature words; add a strip of bubble wrap for sound feedback

games.name: Magic Tissue-Pull Box
props: empty tissue box or wipe box
steps: Stuff the handkerchiefs one by one into the box, leaving one corner peeking out
Demonstrate pulling one out with a surprised face: 'Wow — out it comes!'
Let the baby grab a corner and pull; cheer for every handkerchief extracted
Level up: tie a loose knot in a handkerchief to add pulling resistance
games.goal: Grip strength, bimanual coordination, cause-and-effect experience
games.safety: Use whole cloth squares, not paper tissues (no paper scraps to mouth); put cloths away afterward to prevent entanglement; box opening edges must be smooth
games.extensions: Tie a large bell (over 4cm) to one corner for sound; use cloths of different textures

games.name: Cushion Mountain Climb
steps: Stack cushions on the play mat into a 20-30cm hill
Place a favorite toy on the summit
Encourage the baby to crawl up on all fours to grab the toy
Celebrate with a hug; next round, place the toy a bit farther away
games.goal: Advanced crawling, limb strength, weight-shift control
games.safety: Play mat underneath to cushion falls; hill no higher than baby's sitting height; parent guards from behind against face-plants
games.extensions: Set up two hills with a gap to practice stepping over; parent lies on the mat as a 'human hill'

games.name: Finger-Play for the Road
steps: When the baby in the car seat can see you, raise both hands
Chant a finger play with actions: 'This is Daddy's thumb, Daddy drives the car, beep beep beep'
Tickle the baby's palm or sole lightly at each sound effect for giggles
Repeat slowly, emphasizing the rhyming ends
games.goal: Speech rhythm input, onomatopoeia imitation, calming in the car
games.safety: Performed by a non-driving adult only; never block the driver's view; stop and protect the baby before sudden braking
games.extensions: Swap in slow songs with hand shadows; let the baby grab a parent's finger for a 'pinky promise' interaction

games.name: Friend in the Mirror
props: secure wall mirror or phone front camera
steps: Hold the baby about 50cm in front of the mirror
Point at the reflection and ask 'Who is that?', pause, then answer 'It's baby!'
Make exaggerated faces — smile, surprise, pout — and wait for imitation
Point and name: 'This is baby's nose, this is Mommy's nose'
games.goal: Emerging self-recognition, emotion recognition, social referencing
games.safety: Mirror must be securely fixed and crack-free; parent holds the baby with one arm to prevent lunging forward; avoid harsh glare
games.extensions: Put on a hat or scarf in front of the mirror and watch the reaction; two parents in frame for 'find the family member'

games.name: Bubble Chase Crawl
props: bubble solution (DIY: water + dish soap + a little sugar)
steps: Blow a few bubbles over the grass or play mat
Point them out: 'The bubbles are floating away — go catch them!'
Encourage the baby to crawl toward drifting bubbles and pop them with a hand
Clap and count each pop: 'One, two, three!'
games.goal: Hand-eye coordination in motion, crawling motivation, visual tracking
games.safety: Keep bubble solution away from eyes and mouth; choose flat ground without puddles; sun hat; do not let the child hold the bubble bottle
games.extensions: For older babies, switch to walking after bubbles; use wind direction to make landing spots predictable

games.name: Cup Stacking Tower
steps: Seat the baby in the high chair; demonstrate stacking two cups beside them
Hand over cups one by one, saying 'Higher and higher —'
Gasp with amazement past 4 layers, then count the cups together
Finish with the 'demolition': shout '3, 2, 1, down!' and topple it for a rebuild
games.goal: Precise placement control, hand-eye coordination, early number sense
games.safety: Choose soft-rimmed cups to avoid cuts; cup opening wider than 4cm; pick up fallen cups promptly to prevent slipping
games.extensions: Draw color dots on cups for color matching; build upside-down cup pyramids

games.name: Push-Box Walker
props: sturdy cardboard or storage box (weighted with books)
steps: Load the box so it pushes steadily without sliding away
Clear a 3-4 meter straight runway in the living room
Have the child stand holding the box; back away slowly in front, calling 'Here we go!'
Place a plush at the finish line; arriving and 'delivering' it counts as a win
games.goal: Transition to independent walking, balance and leg strength
games.safety: Box height at chest level and tip-resistant; runway cleared with corner guards on tables; parent alongside at all times
games.extensions: Add curves and 'delivery stops'; place a toy mid-route requiring a squat-and-pickup

games.name: Point-and-Name Story Time
steps: Cuddle up with the book; point out 1-2 items per page
Ask 'Where is the kitty?' and wait for the child to point
Confirm and expand: 'Yes, the kitty — the meow-meow kitty'
Close the book and recap: 'Today we met the elephant and the kitty'
games.goal: Vocabulary comprehension, pointing response, reading habit formation
games.safety: Choose rounded-corner board books; no long reading in dim light; stop as soon as the child rubs their eyes
games.extensions: Shift to 'parent points, child says' expression mode; match book items to real objects at home

games.name: Sock Matching Master
props: 5-6 pairs of clean socks in clearly different colors
steps: Lay out 4-5 single socks on the mat and hold another one
Hold it up and ask, 'Where is its friend?'
If the child grabs any sock, compare: 'Same color? Let's look again'
High-five on a match, then roll pairs into 'sock balls' for storage
games.goal: Color and pattern matching, one-to-one correspondence, self-care seed
games.safety: Put socks away after the game to prevent mouth/nose stuffing; pick socks without detachable decorations
games.extensions: Level up to size ordering; mix in gloves and handkerchiefs for 'which one is not a sock'

games.name: Two-Cup Pouring Station
steps: Set two cups on the tray; fill one a third with lukewarm water
Demonstrate tilting to pour, stressing 'slowly —'
Let the child hold the cup with both hands and try; spills land on the tray, no problem
On success, guide pouring back and forth for repeated practice
games.goal: Wrist control, bimanual teamwork, volume perception
games.safety: Lukewarm water only, never hot; old towels on the floor against slipping; plastic cups only, no glass; wipe spills immediately
games.extensions: Switch to dry beans or quinoa (with constant supervision against tasting under 24m); use a narrow-neck bottle to raise difficulty

games.name: Animal Walk Parade
steps: Announce on the grass: 'Let's walk like animals!'
Demonstrate a waddling duck while quacking; invite the child to follow
Take turns imitating: bunny hops, elephant trunk swing, sideways crab walk
Finish with 'animal commands': call an animal name and the child instantly switches moves
games.goal: Gait variety, balance, imitation and auditory reaction
games.safety: Choose flat grass; parent holds hands for jumping moves; avoid slippery mud and gravel
games.extensions: Add speed words (walk slowly / run fast); hold an 'animal race' to see who reaches the tree first

games.name: Hidden Treasure Cups
steps: While the child watches, hide the toy under one of the cups
Slowly swap cup positions once or twice
Ask 'Where is the toy hiding?' and let the child lift a cup
Cheer on finds; after 3 wins in a row, add more swaps or cups
games.goal: Advanced object permanence, working memory, visual tracking
games.safety: Toy larger than 4cm with no small parts; leave a finger gap when setting cups down to avoid pinches; table corners protected
games.extensions: Hide objects in obvious spots indoors with 'hot/cold' hints; let the child hide and parent seek to practice role reversal

games.name: Kick the Big Ball
props: large beach ball or soft ball
steps: Set the jackets one meter apart as a goal
Place the ball in front of the child and demonstrate kicking toward it
Encourage a step-up-and-kick; cheer and count every goal
Gradually narrow the goal or step back to raise the challenge
games.goal: Single-leg standing balance, eye-foot coordination, goal awareness
games.safety: Use a big light soft ball; open area free of people and obstacles; closed shoes; never kick toward people
games.extensions: Switch to throwing into the goal for upper-body practice; parent plays gentle goalkeeper for interaction

games.name: Face Imitation Show
props: none (phone selfie camera for instant replay optional)
steps: Sit face to face while waiting in line
Parent makes exaggerated faces: big laugh, frown, surprised 'wow', grumpy pout
After each face ask, 'What's Mommy feeling?' and wait for imitation
Name emotions with simple words: 'happy', 'angry', 'surprised'
games.goal: Emotion recognition and naming, facial muscle control, waiting-period soothing
games.safety: Do not linger on negative faces like 'crying' or 'scared'; switch to funny faces if the child gets uneasy
games.extensions: Level up to 'parent says the word, child performs'; match faces on picture-book characters

games.name: Road-Trip Song Relay
steps: Play or sing a familiar nursery rhyme in the car
Pause at keywords and wait for the child to fill in the word
Accept any approximate sound, then restate the correct version and continue
Rotate 2-3 songs and note the child's favorite
games.goal: Word retrieval, sense of rhythm, song memory
games.safety: Run by the adult in the back seat; moderate volume that does not affect driving; pause for rest if the child is fussy
games.extensions: Rewrite lyrics with the child's name; add clapping patterns at double and half speed

games.name: Tape Hopscotch
steps: Tape 3-4 connected squares on the floor
Demonstrate a two-foot jump into the first square shouting 'One!', then the next
Have the child jump through, landing steady before the next square
Level up: jump on command ('jump to the red square'), single-foot hops (32m+)
games.goal: Two-foot jump power, landing balance, number sequence
games.safety: Press tape edges flat to prevent tripping; grip socks or bare feet, no slippers; move furniture for runway space
games.extensions: Tape a maze route to walk within a time limit; place action cards in squares (squat once / spin around) to draw and perform

games.name: Sock-Ball Bowling
steps: Fill bottles about one-fifth with water and set them in a triangle
Mark a throwing line with tape two meters away
Demonstrate an underhand toss at the pins, shouting 'Down —!'
Take turns, count the pins knocked down, and re-rack together
games.goal: Throwing force and direction control, counting practice, turn-taking rules
games.safety: Plastic bottles only, no glass; no people or breakables in the throwing lane; watch footing when retrieving the ball
games.extensions: Move the line farther; switch to overhand throws; write numbers on bottles and add scores for early addition

games.name: Little Kitchen Helper
steps: Put an apron on the child and assign the job: 'Today you are in charge of washing the veggies'
Demonstrate tearing lettuce into large pieces and rinsing them in the basin
As the child tears and washes, narrate: 'One piece, two pieces... rinse the bubbles off'
At dinner announce formally: 'This dish was made with our helper's help!'
games.goal: Finger strength, sense of task completion, chores participation and responsibility
games.safety: Keep away from stove, knives and hot water; work surface height safe from reaching hazards; separate raw and washed; wash hands after
games.extensions: Level up to shelling peas or cracking eggs (parent holds the bowl); after meals the child wipes their own small table

games.name: Color Treasure Hunt
steps: Show a color card and announce the mission: 'Find 3 red things'
Hunt around the neighborhood: red flowers, a red bike, a red door plaque
Repeat and confirm each find: 'This is red — well spotted!'
Switch colors after completing one; spread out the haul at home and count it
games.goal: Color generalization, observational search, categorization
games.safety: Do not pick up sharp, dirty or unknown berries; stay within one arm's reach of the caregiver; keep away from driveways and water
games.extensions: Switch to shapes (round/square); restrict to 'leaves only' for a nature collection book

games.name: Picture-Story Making
props: wordless picture book or 3-4 picture cards
steps: Open a page and ask, 'What is happening in the picture?'
Expand any words the child says into a full sentence: 'Yes, the bear is — chasing a butterfly!'
Probe details: 'Why is the bear chasing it?' 'What happens next?'
Weave the child's contributions into a mini story credited to them: 'The story by...'
games.goal: Narrative expression, imagination and inference, sentence expansion
games.safety: Soft adequate lighting; keep under 10 minutes to protect sleep readiness; if the child gets overexcited, parent narrates instead
games.extensions: Act the story out with plush toys; 'serialize' it the next night with a sequel

games.name: Feed and Care for Baby Doll
steps: Set the scene: 'The dolly is hungry and sleepy — let's take care of her'
Guide pretend feeding with the small spoon, adding sound effects: 'Yum — so tasty'
After feeding, pat the back, tuck the blanket, whisper a lullaby with a finger to lips: 'Shh'
Wrap up with a review: 'You took such good care of the dolly, just like Mommy takes care of you'
games.goal: Empathy and caregiving behavior, role immersion, daily-routine memory
games.safety: All props larger than 4cm against choking; no real food; never actually cover the doll's mouth and nose during the lullaby demo
games.extensions: Add a 'dolly is sick' scenario with pretend temperature checks; introduce queuing at the pretend doctor for role rotation

games.name: Fruit Cutting Fun
steps: Peel the banana onto the board; demonstrate pressing the safe knife gently to slice while holding with the other hand
Hand-over-hand for 1-2 slices, then let the child try independently
Count while cutting: 'One slice, two slices... five in total!'
Plate the slices for the family to share and thank the little chef
games.goal: Bimanual division of labor, pressure control, counting in action
games.safety: Blunt plastic knife only; parent stays at the same side without leaving; damp cloth under the board to prevent slipping; put the knife away right after
games.extensions: Try softer avocado/strawberry; level up to spreading jam on bread with a butter knife

games.name: Size Line-Up
props: 3-5 caps or toy cars of different sizes (keep in the bag)
steps: Set the items out on a small table or your lap while waiting
Ask: 'Which is the biggest? Which is the smallest?' and let the child point
Guide ordering from big to small, chanting 'big, smaller, smallest'
Shuffle and reorder in reverse, or stack them vertically into a 'tower' to verify the order
games.goal: Size comparison and seriation, visual discrimination, waiting-time focus
games.safety: Items larger than 4cm against choking; do not play with shared public objects; pack up to avoid tripping others
games.extensions: Switch to ordering by length (straw segments); introduce 'the one in the middle' for ordinal positions

games.name: Great Sound Guess
steps: Announce in the car: 'Guess what this sound is?'
Parent makes sounds: claps, tongue clicks, cat meows, car 'beep beep'
After the child guesses, swap roles — child makes sounds, parent guesses, deliberately wrong for laughs
Level up: two sounds in a row — 'Which came first, which came second?'
games.goal: Auditory discrimination and memory, word retrieval, sequence memory
games.safety: Played with the back-seat adult; no startling noises that distract driving; wind down when the child gets drowsy
games.extensions: Improvise with real sounds outside (horns/rain/radio); replay recordings and guess 'whose voice is in the family'

games.name: Carrying Bag Champion
steps: Set a 'home base' at each end of the grass; put the bucket at one end
Scatter 5 beanbags across the middle section
The child sets off with the bag and picks up the beanbags one by one
Carry them back and pour into the bucket; cheer when all are delivered, then race the clock for another round
games.goal: Loaded-walking balance, squat-to-grasp combination, task persistence
games.safety: Keep the load light (under 500g total); flat ground without holes; route within parent's sight; hydrate and rest as needed
games.extensions: Walk balancing a beanbag on the head; hop on one foot to each beanbag before picking up; carry only the color called out

games.name: Indoor Obstacle Course
steps: Design four stations: (1) crawl through the blanket 'bridge' between two chairs (2) three two-foot jumps on cushions (3) walk the tape 'balance beam' (4) carry a ping-pong ball on a spoon to the finish
Demonstrate a full run and time it
The child runs station by station with retries allowed; parent acts as 'commentator'
Chase a personal best, or take turns racing the parents
games.goal: Motor planning, body control, rule-following and frustration tolerance
games.safety: Chairs stable and non-wobbling with mats along the route; pick up dropped ping-pong balls immediately to avoid slipping; rest spots between stations; no countdown-pressure stations
games.extensions: Let the child design a fifth station; blindfold walk on the tape guided by parent voice commands (trust practice)

games.name: Paper-Cutting Workshop
steps: Demonstrate correct scissor grip: thumb in one hole, index and middle in the other
Start with straight lines: draw thick lines and cut along them into strips
Move on to curves and zigzags to cut 'grass' and 'waves'
Fold paper, cut notches, unfold into window flowers and display on the glass
games.goal: Scissor bimanual mechanics, cutting along lines, symmetry concept
games.safety: Child-safe round-tip scissors only; cut seated and never walk with scissors; clear scraps promptly; scissors returned to parents after use
games.extensions: Cut symmetric hearts for a greeting card; challenge a hanging spiral paper snake

games.name: Word Chain Road Trip
steps: Explain the rule: the next word starts with the last sound of the previous word, e.g. 'cat — tea — ice'
Relax the rule for younger kids: rhyming links also count; adults judge flexibly
Take turns; whoever gets stuck performs a mini show (a song or an animal sound)
Play 3 rounds, record the longest chain of the trip, and beat it next ride
games.goal: Word retrieval speed, phonological awareness, turn-taking and memory
games.safety: Played with the non-driving adult; do not compete with navigation audio; pause if the banter gets heated
games.extensions: Theme-restricted chains (animals/food only); switch to antonyms or same-category rapid fire

games.name: Sock Puppet Theater
steps: Decorate old socks into characters together: draw eyes, sew ears, give each a name
Drape a bed sheet over the sofa back as a stage curtain
Parent opens with a short scene: 'Bunny lost her carrot — who will help?'
Invite the child's puppet to continue the ending; the whole family takes the stage
games.goal: Narrative creation, dialogue turn-taking, emotional expression and rehearsed conflict resolution
games.safety: Buttons and small decorations must be sewn tight or drawn instead; clear the stage area against tripping; keep plots free of scary elements
games.extensions: Record the 'show' and replay to review lines; script a 'problem play' from the child's real day to discuss solutions

games.name: Baking Little Mathematician
steps: Pick a simple recipe (banana muffins); the child reads out the ingredient list
Measure with spoons while counting: '2 spoons of sugar — 1, 2'; compare big/medium/small cup marks
Mash bananas and stir the batter, observing how wet and dry mixtures change
Set the oven timer and wonder 'how long is 25 minutes'; split the batch evenly when done — how many each
games.goal: Number-quantity mapping, fair-sharing fractions, sequential execution and waiting
games.safety: Oven and hot pans handled by parents within a marked zone; no tasting raw batter with egg; wash hands after; swap allergens per the child profile
games.extensions: Shape dough into letters/numbers and bake crisp; double the recipe for multiplication (school age); guess-then-weigh with a kitchen scale

games.name: Cooperative Ball Transport
steps: Rule: two people each hold one end of a towel and carry the ball together to a basket 10 meters away — no hands on the ball
Do a slow parent-child trial run and discuss 'how do we keep the ball on'
Start the real challenge; if the ball drops, return to the start
Level up after success: S-curve around obstacles, or 3 balls in a row against the clock
games.goal: Cooperative communication, pace synchronization, frustration tolerance and shared goals
games.safety: Flat ground, yield to pedestrians; watch for other runners when retrieving the ball; hydrate and wear hats in hot weather
games.extensions: Three-person, two-board relay; switch to carrying soaked sponges and compare water at the finish

games.name: Silent Sound Detective
steps: Announce the '30-second silence' challenge: eyes closed or heads down, ears only
Parent makes soft sounds from different spots in the waiting area (jiggling keys, finger snaps)
The child opens their eyes and points out the direction and the object
Swap roles: parent closes eyes while the child makes gentle sounds to test the parent
games.goal: Auditory attention and orientation, environmental sound discrimination, self-control (staying quiet)
games.safety: Choose a quiet waiting area without disturbing others; parent holds hands when eyes are closed; no audio sources pressed to ears
games.extensions: Checklist bingo of ambient sounds (announcements/footsteps/ringtones); advanced: 'how many kinds of sounds in 30 seconds'

games.name: Number Long-Jump Open
steps: Draw a take-off line and numbered squares 1-8 ahead (30cm spacing, increasing)
Standing long jump — the landing square is your score
Add up 3 jumps for a total; parents play by the same rules
Log today's personal best and challenge the record next time
games.goal: Standing long-jump power and landing cushioning, cumulative addition, goal tracking
games.safety: Dry flat ground or grass; sports shoes; demonstrate bent-knee landings to protect knees; stop when tired (max 10 jumps per set)
games.extensions: Single-leg version; 'backward jump minus points' variant to practice subtraction; estimate 'how far I'll reach' before each jump, then verify

games.name: Bedtime Story Chain
steps: Dim to a night light and lie down; parent opens: 'Once upon a time, a kitten wanted to see the stars in daylight...'
Stop after two sentences: 'What happened next? Your turn'
Accept whatever the child offers and nudge along with questions: 'So what did the kitten do?'
Bring the plot to a calm close: 'The kitten fell asleep — let's sleep too'
games.goal: Improvised narrative, listening and continuity, language fluency
games.safety: No monsters or scary-dark elements; gradually lower your voice toward sleep; if the child gets wired, parent solo-narrates the ending
games.extensions: Keep one 'serial hero' with nightly sequels; on weekends draw the week's story as a four-panel comic

games.name: Shadow Tag
steps: In a sunny open space, observe together: 'Where are the shadows? Do they move?'
Rules: stomp only on the other person's shadow while protecting your own
One-minute chases; after 3 tags, swap the runner
Overtime rule: shadows 'hiding' in tree shade count as a safe zone
games.goal: Cutting runs and quick stops, space and light-shadow cognition, reaction speed
games.safety: Avoid midday sun (choose morning/late afternoon); open ground without stones or puddles; parent paces the chase to prevent overexertion
games.extensions: Play at morning vs. evening to compare shadow length and direction; strike poses to 'paste' shadows on a wall for a shadow-puppet show

games.name: Family Orienteering Hunt
steps: Parent hides sticky-note 'control markers' at 4-5 spots in advance and draws a simple map
Hand over the map and first clue; the child plans the visiting order
Check in at each point by copying the word or answering the math puzzle on the note
Reunite at the finish to verify the punch record; score time plus accuracy; rotate who sets the course
games.goal: Map reading and sense of direction, route planning, endurance and execution
games.safety: Markers in public areas within parental sight; no watersides, garages or dense woods; agree on a lost-meet point; cancel in bad weather
games.extensions: Upgrade with a compass; switch to a glow-stick night hunt with parents alongside; child designs the course to stump the parents

games.name: Paper Bridge Engineer
props: coins or a small bag as weights
steps: Challenge: build a bridge spanning 20cm using only 2 A4 sheets — whoever holds the most weight wins
Sketch the design first: flat deck? corrugated folds? triangular truss?
Build within 15 minutes; the deck must be able to hold coins
Load coins one by one until collapse, record the count, discuss 'why do folds make it stronger', then iterate and rematch
games.goal: Structural engineering thinking, shape-strength relationships, iterative improvement and quantitative comparison
games.safety: Scissor discipline; testing area away from eyes; sweep up coins after collapse to prevent slips; do not build on tall book stacks that may topple
games.extensions: 'Less paper, same load' challenge; upgrade to a paper tower height contest; look up photos of real truss bridges to compare

games.name: Three-Minute Mini Debate
steps: Draw a relatable topic: 'play first or homework first', 'cats vs dogs'
Rock-paper-scissors for sides — you may land the side you disagree with (more fun)
One minute of statements each plus two minutes of open crossfire; parent referees
Award 'the most convincing line' and discuss: which point from the other side was actually strong
games.goal: Organizing and voicing opinions, listening and rebuttal, perspective-taking and rules
games.safety: Avoid topics touching raw family conflicts; pause if crossfire turns into quarrels; debrief 'critique the idea, not the person'
games.extensions: Add a 3-minute 'fact-check window' to prep with sources; three-player 'carousel debate' version

games.name: Kitchen Science Lab
steps: Experiment 1 'volcano': 2 spoons of baking soda plus coloring on the plate; pour vinegar and watch it erupt
Predict first, verify later: write down 'what I think will happen', then compare with the result
Experiment 2 'density rainbow': pour honey, water, then oil into one cup and watch the layers
Summarize the principles: acid-base reaction makes gas / liquids of different densities; write a one-page lab report
games.goal: Hypothesis-verification scientific method, observation and recording, causal attribution
games.safety: Parent supervises throughout; keep the reaction away from eyes and face; never taste any experiment material; clean surfaces and hands thoroughly afterwards
games.extensions: Variable testing: compare eruption height vs. baking soda amount; add a 'float or sink prediction list' of household items; rigorous version weighs everything on a kitchen scale

games.name: Long-Rope Team Jumping
props: 1-2 long jump ropes (a chalk line can simulate one)
steps: Two parents (or one parent plus a tree) turn the rope; first watch the rhythm chanting '1-2-in'
The child learns to time entry by rope sound; first goal is 5 clean jumps
Level up to two jumpers together, then 8-figure run-throughs (in — jump — out — to the queue)
Team challenge: 20 unbroken jumps as a group, with chants to stay in sync
games.goal: Rhythm and timing, lower-limb endurance, team chemistry and a cheering culture
games.safety: Flat ground free of gravel; exclusive rope zone to avoid tripping passers-by; sports shoes and snug clothing; build up gradually weekly to protect ankles — stop at any ankle pain
games.extensions: Criss-cross and double-unders; family 'jump relay' of 10 each; weekly count leaderboard

games.name: Back-Seat Navigator
steps: Before departure, show the full route and mark the start, the finish and 2-3 towns along the way
En route the navigator announces each upcoming turn (left/right) and highway exits
Check predictions against the phone navigation — being wrong is fine; review why
On arrival, trace the actual route in pencil and estimate 'how far did we go'
games.goal: Direction and route cognition, map-symbol understanding, sustained attention and responsibility
games.safety: Navigation tips are for the accompanying adult only — the driver's decisions prevail; no quizzing while the driver is busy; stop map reading on bumpy roads against motion sickness
games.extensions: Estimate 'how much longer' using distance and speed; let the navigator manage rest-stop decisions

games.name: Ten-Minute Evening Journal
steps: Fixed bedtime ritual: write 'three lines for today' — happiest moment, one new thing learned, one wish for tomorrow
Younger grades can mix pinyin and drawings; parents take no dictation and do not write for them
Add a small illustration or stickers to decorate the day's page
At month's end, flip back to the first page and look together at 'me, one month ago'
games.goal: Written expression, self-review and emotional sorting, habit persistence
games.safety: Soft non-glaring light (eye protection); close the notebook after 15 minutes — no late nights; respect privacy — never read and criticize entries without permission
games.extensions: Write letters to future self, sealed quarterly; travel journal specials (ticket stubs + map clippings)

games.name: Design Your Own Board Game
steps: Kick-off: pick a theme (zoo adventure / school treasure hunt) and the win condition
Draw the board: a 20-30 space path with forward/backward/event squares, and write the event cards
Set the rules: starting resources per player and event resolution; condense into a one-page 'manual'
Family playtest — patch any loopholes you find, revise the rules, and play again
games.goal: Rule design and logical consistency, balance intuition, negotiation and iteration
games.safety: Put scissors and rulers away after use; dice and caps over 4cm, stored safely if younger siblings are around; avoid harsh punishment mechanics that spark big conflicts
games.extensions: Add a token economy (chores earn coins for privileges); record a 'release video' pitching the rules

games.name: Twenty Questions
steps: The quizzer thinks of one thing (category limited first: animal / food / household object)
The guesser may ask up to 20 questions answerable only with yes or no
Teach questioning strategy: start with broad categories ('Is it an animal?') then narrow ('Does it live in water?')
Rotate quizzer over 3 rounds and track the 'fewest questions' record
games.goal: Classification and binary-split logic, questioning strategy, information compression
games.safety: Played with the non-driving adult; drop disputed answers and move on; keep rounds light if motion sickness appears
games.extensions: Theme editions (historical figures / book characters only); reverse mode: quizzer may only answer yes/no/maybe for extra difficulty

games.name: Timed Chore Challenge
steps: Write task cards into a bowl: wipe the table, set the table, toy-zone cleanup, water the plants, sweep 5 square meters
Draw a card and start the timer: 'Table-wiping mission — done within 10 minutes!'
Log the time on completion; compete against personal history, not family members' speed
Ten check-ins in a week earn a 'family privilege' (such as picking the weekend movie)
games.goal: Family responsibility sharing, task breakdown and time estimation, delayed gratification
games.safety: No tasks involving knives or hot water; cleaning agents stored and used by parents; no climbing tasks; keep the vibe light, no pressure
games.extensions: 'Co-op deep clean' with the whole family racing zones for 30 minutes; let the child be 'chore manager' for a week — scheduling and inspecting
